prompt:
Find real, published data on how often prediction markets (Polymarket, Kalshi or similar) resolve disputed or ambiguous markets, or how many market resolutions were challenged. Cite the sources and quote the figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here is published data on how often prediction-market resolutions are challenged or disputed. Note that nearly all quantitative data available covers Polymarket (whose UMA-oracle disputes are recorded on-chain and publicly auditable); Kalshi publishes no dispute feed, so no equivalent challenge rate exists for it.

SOURCE: https://bullpenbrief.com/how-often-do-polymarket-markets-end-in-dispute-we-analyzed-143000/ | QUOTE: "Of 143,286 Polymarket markets resolved from March 2025 to August 2026 (Polymarket gamma API, UMA oracle status), 545 or 0.38%, about 1 in 263, ended in a formal resolution dispute." | CLAIM: Across ~143,000 resolved Polymarket markets, 0.38% (545 markets, roughly 1 in 263) ended in a formal resolution dispute.

SOURCE: https://bullpenbrief.com/how-often-do-polymarket-markets-end-in-dispute-we-analyzed-143000/ | QUOTE: "Polymarket markets with more than $100,000 in trading volume were disputed 1.45% of the time (1 in 69), about 11 times the 0.13% rate for markets under $1,000 (143,286 markets, 2025 to 2026)." | CLAIM: Dispute rates rise sharply with trading volume — high-volume markets (>$100k) were disputed 1.45% of the time, ~11× the rate of sub-$1,000 markets.

SOURCE: https://bullpenbrief.com/how-often-do-polymarket-markets-end-in-dispute-we-analyzed-143000/ | QUOTE: "Political and election markets on Polymarket were disputed 1.89% of the time (1 in 53), about 16 times the 0.12% rate for crypto markets (markets resolved March 2025 to August 2026)." | CLAIM: Dispute frequency varies strongly by category; political/election markets dispute at 1.89% versus 0.12% for crypto markets.

SOURCE: https://bullpenbrief.com/how-often-do-polymarket-markets-end-in-dispute-we-analyzed-143000/ | QUOTE: "The largest disputed Polymarket market by volume was the $242 million “Will Zelenskyy wear a suit before July?” contract (June 2025); all five largest disputed markets were political or geopolitical." | CLAIM: The biggest disputed market on record had $242M in volume, and the five largest disputed markets were all political/geopolitical.

SOURCE: https://vultax.com/research/how-long-polymarket-takes-to-settle-markets | QUOTE: "Disputes were rare: 89 markets, 0.08%." | CLAIM: In a 15 August–10 September 2026 sample of 110,576 Polymarket markets, only 89 (0.08%) were disputed.

SOURCE: https://vultax.com/research/how-long-polymarket-takes-to-settle-markets | QUOTE: "Markets that traded $100,000 or more were disputed six times as often, 0.5%, and geopolitics markets, whose questions meet messy events, 3.5% of the time, with a median wait of 74 hours after their scheduled end." | CLAIM: Larger markets were disputed at 0.5% (6× the overall rate) and geopolitics markets at 3.5% — the highest category rate in that window.

SOURCE: https://vultax.com/research/how-long-polymarket-takes-to-settle-markets | QUOTE: "Anyone can dispute by posting a matching bond; a first dispute triggers a fresh proposal, and a second sends the question to a vote of UMA token holders, a discussion period of 24 to 48 hours followed by a vote of about 48 hours." | CLAIM: Describes Polymarket's formal dispute/challenge mechanism (bond-posted challenges escalating to a UMA token-holder vote).

SOURCE: https://clearmarket.fyi/research/resolution-clarity-index/ | QUOTE: "Across 7,166 Polymarket markets with public dispute records, contracts ClearMarket rated C (the lowest of its three Resolution Clarity Grades) were formally disputed at 20 times the rate of A- and B-rated contracts (1.59% vs 0.08%)." | CLAIM: Ambiguously-worded contracts (rated "C" for resolution clarity) were disputed at 1.59%, 20× the 0.08% rate of clearly-worded ones — ambiguity is a strong predictor of challenge.

SOURCE: https://clearmarket.fyi/research/resolution-clarity-index/ | QUOTE: "52 of the 55 markets that ended up in a resolution dispute had been rated C by ClearMarket, the lowest clarity tier." | CLAIM: 52 of 55 formally disputed Polymarket markets had been pre-identified as having unclear resolution rules.

SOURCE: https://clearmarket.fyi/research/resolution-clarity-index/ | QUOTE: "The largest to date: Kalshi's February 2026 market on whether Iran's Supreme Leader would leave office, roughly $54M in volume, settled at the last traded price under a death carveout that appeared in the CFTC-filed terms but not on the trading page most traders read." | CLAIM: The largest known contested Kalshi settlement (~$54M volume) resulted from a resolution rule visible in filed terms but not on the trading page.

SOURCE: https://clearmarket.fyi/research/resolution-clarity-index/ | QUOTE: "Kalshi refunded $2.2M in trades and fees, a class action is pending, and the episode forced a new exchange-wide settlement rule." | CLAIM: The disputed Kalshi Iran market resolution led to $2.2M in refunds, a pending class action, and a new settlement rule.

SOURCE: https://fidonis.org/integrity/polymarket/2026-04/ | QUOTE: "From Mar 2025 through Jan 2026, $1502.9M of traded volume passed through a disputed resolution, 7.3% of all UMA-resolved volume." | CLAIM: Volume-weighted, 7.3% of Polymarket's UMA-resolved trading volume (~$1.5 billion) passed through a disputed resolution — far higher than the count-based rate, because disputes cluster in big markets.

SOURCE: https://fidonis.org/integrity/polymarket/2026-04/ | QUOTE: "Count dispute rate 0.33% Jan '26, by market count" | CLAIM: In January 2026, 0.33% of resolved Polymarket markets were disputed (228 of 69,611 markets that month).

SOURCE: https://predictacademy.ai/academy/prediction-market-resolution/ | QUOTE: "More than 1,150 Polymarket markets were disputed in the first five months of 2026 alone, already ahead of the full 2025 total." | CLAIM: Disputes are increasing over time — over 1,150 disputed markets in Jan–May 2026, exceeding all of 2025.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Any comprehensive, independently computable dispute/challenge rate for Kalshi markets. Kalshi publishes no dispute feed; per the ClearMarket source, "Kalshi publishes no dispute feed, so a Kalshi challenge rate cannot be independently computed by anyone, at any standard" — its contested settlements surface only via courts, regulators, and press.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Data on dispute rates for prediction markets other than Polymarket and Kalshi (e.g., Manifold, Metaculus, PredictIt) — no published challenge/ambiguous-resolution statistics for these platforms appeared in the sources.

Brief context for interpretation: the overall Polymarket dispute rate is low by market count (0.08%–0.49% depending on the sample and period), but it is strongly concentrated — high-volume, political, geopolitical, and ambiguously-worded markets dispute at rates from ~1.5% up to 3.5%, and by dollar volume roughly 5–17% of monthly resolved volume has passed through disputed resolutions in some months. Also note that "disputed" in these datasets means a formal on-chain UMA challenge was filed, not that the original outcome was overturned (many challenges fail).
